extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/agents) handling reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for preparing, filing, and examining reissue applications to correct patents (including interactions with reexamination, PTAB proceedings, interferences/derivation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of remarks accompanying an amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Per MPEP §714.16, remarks accompanying an amendment that corrects an error in the patent must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required whenever an amendment to correct an error affects disclosure, claim scope, or adds a claim. The remarks must be complete and clear so the examiner can determine compliance with reissue requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reissue oath/declaration requirements (pre-September 16, 2012 filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration must accompany an amendment submitted after allowance and must state that the error(s) to be corrected arose without any deceptive intention by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental oath/declaration submitted after allowance must be directed only to the error(s) the applicant seeks to correct after allowance; it need not cover earlier errors if those were already covered by a pre-allowance reissue oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections not requiring physical amendment still treated as amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Correcting an error after allowance that does not include an amendment of the specification or claims (e.g., filing a certified copy of an original foreign application) is nevertheless an amendment of the patent for reissue purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when no physical amendment is entered, the requirements of 37 CFR 1.312 and related reissue rules must be met because the correction is treated as an amendment of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standard for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application, including all claims therein, is to be examined in the same manner as a non-reissue, non-provisional application (37 CFR 1.176).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in a reissue application are subject to any and all rejections the examiner deems appropriate regardless of whether they are identical to original patent claims or were raised during prosecution of the patent. Reissue application claims enjoy no presumption of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling of fraud, inequitable conduct, and duty of disclosure issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not investigate or reject reissue applications under 37 CFR 1.56; it will not comment upon duty of disclosure issues brought to attention in reissue applications except to note them in appropriate circumstances. For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012, examination as to lack of deceptive intent continues but without an Office investigation of fraud/inequitable conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant’s statement in the reissue oath/declaration of lack of deceptive intent will be accepted as dispositive except in special circumstances (e.g., an explicit admission or a judicial determination of fraud or inequitable conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling admissions or judicial determinations of fraud/inequitable conduct (pre-September 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission or judicial determination of fraud, inequitable conduct, or violation of the duty of disclosure is a special circumstance where no Office investigation need be made; a rejection should be made using the appropriate form paragraph (14.21.09.fti or 14.22.fti).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions must be explicit and unequivocal and not subject to other interpretation. If applicant provides a reasonable interpretation of the facts that does not support fraud/inequitable conduct, the rejection should be withdrawn. Use 14.21.09.fti for external judicial determinations and 14.22.fti where the application record contains evidence or admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when a protest is filed while patent is in interference or contested case
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protest is filed in a reissue application related to a patent involved in a pending interference or contested case before the PTAB, the reissue application should be referred to the PTAB before considering the protest and taking action on the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In consultation with examiner and PTAB, confirm (A) all parties to the interference/contested case are aware of the reissue filing, and (B) the Office must not allow claims in a reissue that are unpatentable over pending interference counts or found unpatentable in the interference/contested case. Reissue should not be allowed without the PTAB administrative patent judge’s approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and handling of concurrent reissue and reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application and an ex parte or inter partes reexamination proceeding are pending concurrently on the same patent, the examiner should immediately inform their TC TQAS or SPRS and the patent owner must notify the Office of the concurrent proceeding by filing the appropriate Notification of Concurrent Proceedings (37 CFR 1.178(b), 1.565(a), 1.985(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may decide to merge the two proceedings or suspend one. A petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or stay must be filed after the order to reexamine is issued; petitions filed earlier will not be considered or may be expunged. Notify OPLA when appropriate for decisions on merging/staying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when a reexamination or PTAB trial certificate issues while reissue pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination certificate or PTAB trial certificate is to be issued for a patent while a reissue application is pending and will not be merged, the examiner will not act on the reissue application until the certificate issues and publishes; thereafter, the Office resumes examination and typically gives the patent owner two months to amend reissue claims based on the concluded proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims canceled by the certificate are treated as claims lost in litigation. Further prosecution is generally limited to claims narrower than those canceled; claims equal or broader in scope are generally deemed surrendered and will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 and may be subject to estoppel (see MPEP §2308.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions allowing broader claims after a certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader claims in a reissue application may be presented despite a certificate canceling claims when: (a) the broader claims can be patentable despite the canceled claims (e.g., have an earlier effective filing date or can be sworn behind), and (b) the broader claims could not have been presented in the reexamination or PTAB trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion (a) examples: reissue claims supported by a parent application giving an earlier effective date, or subject matter that can be sworn behind. Criterion (b) example: claims directed to a distinct invention broader than all claims during reexamination/PTAB trial. If all patent claims were canceled, petitions (37 CFR 1.183 or 1.182 depending on context) may be required to proceed; see MPEP for petition procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding when all patent claims are canceled by a certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where all patent claims were canceled by a reexamination certificate or a PTAB trial certificate, the reissue application can proceed to correct the 35 U.S.C. 251 “error” of presenting unpatentable claims, subject to petitions and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims were canceled in a reexamination certificate, the patent owner must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to waive 37 CFR 1.570 and/or 1.997(d) as appropriate; if canceled in a PTAB trial certificate, file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182. A petition is grantable if reissue claims are narrower than canceled claims or satisfy the exceptions described for presenting broader claims (earlier effective date, cannot be sworn behind, or could not have been presented in the other proceeding). Matters may be forwarded to OPLA for resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for suggesting an interference (37 CFR 41.202) in a reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant (including a reissue applicant) suggesting an interference must: (1) identify the application or patent that is the subject of the suggested interference; (2) identify all claims believed to interfere; (3) propose one or more counts and show correspondence of claims to counts; (4) explain in detail why the applicant will prevail on priority; (5) if a claim has been added/amended to provoke an interference, provide a claim chart showing written description support; and (6) for each constructive reduction to practice for which benefit is sought, provide a chart showing where the disclosure provides such reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail (claim charts, correspondence) to satisfy 37 CFR 41.202 and the case law cited (e.g., In re Keil, In re Dien). These materials substantiate the basis for the suggested interference and priority assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority to require adding a claim to provoke an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may require an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference; failure to satisfy the requirement within a period set by the examiner (not less than one month) operates as a concession of priority for that subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the interference would be with a patent, the reissue applicant must also comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a)(2)–(a)(6). The proposed claim must be patentable to the applicant (apart from priority issues) and must be drawn to patentable subject matter claimed by another applicant or patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using a reissue application to provoke an interference: conditions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application may be employed to provoke an interference if it (A) adds copied claims not present in the original patent, (B) amends claims to correspond to those of the patent/application with which an interference is sought, or (C) contains at least one error appropriate for reissue (not directed solely to provoking an interference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For situations (A) and (B), the reissue oath/declaration must assert that applicant erred in failing to include claims of the proper scope in the original application and identify the claims added to provoke the interference. The subject matter of copied/amended claims must be supported by the original patent disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. A reissue applicant cannot present added/amended claims to provoke an interference if the claims were deliberately omitted from the original patent (for reissues filed before Sept 16, 2012). Timing limits apply (e.g., pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 135(b) and two-year rule under 35 U.S.C. 251) — see MPEP §715.05 and §1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement when a reissue is filed while patent is in interference
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application is filed while the original patent is in an interference proceeding, the reissue applicant must promptly notify the PTAB of the filing within 20 days from the filing date (37 CFR 41.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notification obligation helps ensure coordination between reissue prosecution and interference proceedings and compliance with mandatory notice rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application and derivation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications subject to derivation proceedings (AIA-era 35 U.S.C. 102), a reissue applicant may file a petition to institute a derivation proceeding (see 37 CFR 42.402).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing of derivation proceedings follows the rules in MPEP §2310 and the AIA-era derivation regulations; consider overlap/coordination with reissue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction and election of species in reissue applications; disclaimer consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.176(b), the examiner may require restriction/election between subject matter of the original patent claims and newly added previously unclaimed subject matter; if restriction is required, original patent claims will be held to be constructively elected unless a disclaimer of all original patent claims is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a restriction is made, the Office action should (1) notify of the restriction requirement, (2) hold added claims constructively non-elected and withdrawn from consideration, (3) treat original patent claims on the merits, and (4) inform applicant that if original claims are found allowable and no error (other than failure to present non-elected claims) is being corrected, action will be suspended pending a divisional reissue on the non-elected claims. A disclaimer of all original patent claims, if filed before the Office action treating original claims on the merits, will make only the added claims present for examination; such a disclaimer cannot be withdrawn. Cancellation of all original patent claims is not equivalent to a disclaimer and will not have the same effect.
